questions.answer: `@dec` is sugar for `func = dec(func)`: decorator receives original, returns wrapper replacing it. Wrapper typically closes over func. Decoration runs at definition; wrapper body runs per call.

questions.answer: Closure = inner remembers outer vars after outer returns (e.g. multiplier(2) remembers x=2). Decorators rely on it: wrapper remembers func/config. Generic wrapper needs *args/**kwargs to forward any signature and must return result.
questions.question: Explain closures and why decorator wrappers use *args/**kwargs.

questions.answer: Without @wraps, wrapper replaces metadata (__name__='wrapper', lost doc). Add `@wraps(func)`. Decorator-with-args needs 3 layers: factory(config) -> decorator(func) -> wrapper(*a,**k). Stacking applies bottom-up, executes top-down.
